newsitem.title: USA: CME, Deutsche Boerse to cooperate in DAX trading.
newsitem.headline: CME, Deutsche Boerse to cooperate in DAX trading.

text.p: The Chicago Mercantile Exchange and Deutsche Boerse, the operating company of the Deutsche Terminboerse (DTB), agreed to allow U.S. member firms to trade DAX stock index futures on the CME floor using DTB terminals, the CME and Deutsche Boerse said.
"It (the agreement) translates to easy access to an outstanding product for CME members," CME chairman Jack Sandner said in a statement released jointly by the exchanges.
The CME and Deutsche Boerse hope to install terminals in CME member booths early in the first quarter of 1997, they said. The DTB is Germany's futures and options exchange.

"For the DTB, the agreement opens up a broad membership base in the U.S. which is highly experienced in trading stock index futures," Joerg Franke, executive board member of Deutsche Boerse, said in the joint statement.
DAX, or Deutsche Aktienindex, is a performance index of 30 German blue-chip stocks.
The DTB was the first non-U.S. exchange to receive approval from the U.S. Commodity Futures Trading Commission to install computer trading terminals in the United States.
By the end of 1996, three U.S. member firms were trading DAX stock index futures through DTB terminals. Seven more member firms have applied for DTB membership.

A CME spokeswoman said the exchange would notify the CFTC about their agreement with Deutsche Boerse, but did not believe the agreement was subject to regulatory approval. ((Derivatives desk 312-408-8750;E-mail derivatives@reuters.com))
